name: ipf_nat6_icmperror
prose: ipf_nat6_icmperror(fin, nflags, dir) fixes up an incoming ICMPv6 error packet whose embedded (offending) IPv6 packet belongs to an existing NAT entry. It returns NULL, with *nflags untouched and nothing modified, in two cases: fin->fin_flx has FI_SHORT or FI_FRAGBODY set (statistics counter ns_icmp_short is bumped), or fin->fin_v != 6 or ipf_nat6_icmperrorlookup(fin, dir) returns NULL (ns_icmp_notfound is bumped). Otherwise it sets *nflags = IPN_ICMPERR and always rewrites the embedded packet's ip6_src and ip6_dst from the entry: when (fin_out == 0 and the entry is NAT_MAP) or (fin_out == 1 and the entry is NAT_REDIRECT) they are set to the entry's original source and destination (nat_osrc6, nat_odst6), otherwise to nat_ndst6 (as source) and nat_nsrc6 (as destination). If the embedded next header is TCP or UDP and at least 4 bytes of it are present (dlen >= 4), the embedded source and destination ports are also rewritten from the entry (original or new ports to match the address choice), and the embedded TCP/UDP checksum is adjusted with ipf_fix_datacksum only when the embedded UDP has dlen >= 8 and a non-zero checksum, or the embedded TCP has dlen >= 18; when the embedded checksum is not adjusted, the port delta is accumulated into sumd2 instead. The outer ICMPv6 checksum is adjusted with ipf_fix_incksum only in this TCP/UDP branch, and only if sumd or sumd2 is non-zero and the final sumd2 is non-zero. If the embedded next header is ICMPv6 and at least 8 bytes are present, then only when the direction test selected the 'original' side (odst == 1) and the embedded ICMPv6 id differs from nat_osport, the embedded ICMPv6 id is replaced with nat_oicmpid and the embedded ICMPv6 checksum is compensated via ipf_fix_datacksum; the outer ICMPv6 checksum is not modified in this branch. Other embedded protocols get only the address rewrite. On every non-NULL path it returns the nat_t found by ipf_nat6_icmperrorlookup; this function takes no lock and does not itself release or acquire a reference on it.
note: reviewer 2 right: outer ICMPv6 checksum is only touched in the TCP/UDP branch (ip_nat6.c:1783), the ICMP-query branch (1787-1819) only fixes the embedded id and checksum; also prose omitted dlen/odst conditions

name: ipf_p_raudio_in
prose: ipf_p_raudio_in(arg, fin, aps, nat) is the RealAudio proxy handler for packets coming back from the server; it returns 0 on every return statement in the function (lines 197, 206, 222, 238, 246 and the final return), so its return value does not distinguish cases. It does nothing if rap->rap_sdone is already set, if there is no TCP payload (dlen <= 0), if the first-seen sequence is not yet established and the string 'PNA' is not found in the payload (memstr), if the packet's sequence number is beyond the 19-byte capture window (seq > rap_sseq + sizeof(rap_svr)), or if the 19-byte server reply (rap_sbf == 0x7ffff) together with the end-of-start-messages flag rap_eos has not yet been seen. Along the way it copies up to 19 payload bytes into rap->rap_svr and sets bits in rap_sbf. Once the 19 bytes are complete and rap_eos is set, it sets rap_sdone = 1 and, if the reply carries RA_ID_ROBUST at offset 11, stores the robust UDP port in rap_srport. It then temporarily rewrites the IP header (protocol set to UDP, source = nat_ndstip, destination = nat_odstip, length = header plus a TCP header), builds a pseudo packet descriptor fi on a copy of fin, and for RAP_M_UDP_ROBUST mode with a non-zero rap_srport and for RAP_M_UDP mode it creates a slave UDP NAT entry with ipf_nat_add (called while holding softn->ipf_nat_new, released right after), and when the entry is created calls ipf_nat_proto, ipf_nat_update under nat2->nat_lock, and ipf_state_add. NAT and state creation failures are ignored. At the end it restores ip_p, ip_len, ip_src and ip_dst of the original packet; early returns happen before the header is modified.
note: slice cut the head: function is ipf_p_raudio_in (ip_raudio_pxy.c:170). Old prose 'always returns 0 / header restored' is true for the whole function but described only the tail

name: ipf_state_tcpinwindow
prose: ipf_state_tcpinwindow(fin, fdata, tdata, tcp, flags) decides whether a TCP segment is inside the tracked window of a state entry; fdata is the sender's data block and tdata the peer's. It returns 1 if the segment is accepted and 0 if it is rejected. Before any decision it computes the (scaled) window, treating a zero window as 1, and may update fdata state: on a non-SYN packet with TCP_WSCALE_FIRST set it clears that flag and sets fdata->td_maxwin to the window; and if fdata->td_end == 0 and either IS_TCPFSM is not set in flags or the packet has both SYN and ACK, it initialises fdata->td_end, td_maxwin = 1 and td_maxend. Return 0 paths: (a) IS_STRICT set in flags and seq != fdata->td_end: iss_tcp_strict is bumped, FI_OOW is set in fin->fin_flx; (b) the packet matches none of the acceptance tests: iss_oow is bumped and FI_OOW is set. Return 1 happens when 'inseq' is set by any of: the normal window test (td_maxend >= end, seq >= td_end - maxwin, and the ack skew within MAXACKWINDOW bounds); the SACK case (seq == td_maxend, ackskew == 0, both sides TCP_SACK_PERMIT), which bumps iss_winsack; the RST|ACK case with seq == 0 and ackskew in [-1, 1]; or, only when IS_TCPFSM is not set and neither TCP_WSCALE_SEEN nor TCP_WSCALE_FIRST is set on fdata, the extra guesses (seq == td_maxend with ackskew == 0, or seq + maxwin >= td_end - maxwin). On return 1 it updates tdata->td_end = ack if ackskew < 0, fdata->td_maxwin if the window grew, fdata->td_end if end is beyond it, and tdata->td_maxend if ack + win >= td_maxend, and leaves fin_flx unchanged. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: reviewer round2 right (winsack bumped on return 1 path); round15 right (missed !IS_TCPFSM extra-guess return-1 paths); ip_state.c:2188-2224

name: ipf_tcp_age
prose: ipf_tcp_age(tqe, fin, tqtab, flags, ok) runs the TCP state machine for the direction fin->fin_rev of timeout-queue entry tqe. It reads the old state of the other direction (ostate) and the current state of this direction (nstate), and uses the TCP flags of the packet. The caller is expected to hold the lock on the parent of tqe. It computes an internal result rval: 0 means the flag/state combination is not allowed, 1 means allowed with a transition (or confirmation) of the queue, 2 means allowed without touching the queue. If the packet has RST, nstate becomes CLOSED when the packet has no PUSH flag and no payload, otherwise CLOSE_WAIT; and if ostate <= ESTABLISHED, tqe_state[1 - dir] is set to CLOSE_WAIT immediately (even if ok is 0); rval = 1. Otherwise a switch on the current state gives: LISTEN accepts SYN|ACK (to SYN_RECEIVED) or SYN (to SYN_SENT), and, when IS_TCPFSM is not set in flags, a bare ACK guess depending on ostate; SYN_SENT, SYN_RECEIVED, HALF_ESTAB, ESTABLISHED, CLOSE_WAIT, FIN_WAIT_1 and CLOSING move as the flags dictate (rval 2 for a retransmitted SYN in SYN_SENT or SYN|ACK in SYN_RECEIVED); LAST_ACK accepts only packets with ACK (no state change); TIME_WAIT gives CLOSED and rval 1 if ostate is LAST_ACK and rval 2 otherwise; CLOSED gives rval 2; FIN_WAIT_2 and any unknown state leave rval 0. Finally, rval 2 is converted to 1 with no queue update; for rval 1, tqe_state[dir] is set to nstate only if ok is non-zero, and unless TQE_RULEBASED is set in tqe_flags the entry is moved with ipf_movequeue to tqtab + nstate (this move happens even when ok is 0). It returns 1 for rval 1 or 2, and 0 for rval 0, in which case tqe_state[dir] is not stored and the entry is not moved.
note: slice cut the head: function is ipf_tcp_age (ip_state.c:3933); old prose listed LAST_ACK/FIN_WAIT_2/unknown as the only 0 cases, but LISTEN/SYN_SENT/etc. with non-matching flags also return 0, and ok only gates the state store, not the queue move

name: _n##_rb_insert
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_insert(head, node), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns void. It sets node's left and right links to the sentinel _n##_rb_zero, walks down from the root (head->top._f.right) comparing with _cmp(node, n), going left when the result is negative and right otherwise (so equal keys go to the right), and links node at the leaf position found with colour red and the last visited node as parent. It then restores the red-black properties with the usual recolouring and rotate_left/rotate_right steps while the parent is red, forces the root colour to black, and increments head->count. It has no failure path, does not check for duplicates, allocates or frees nothing and takes no lock. node must not already be linked, head must have been initialised with _n##_rb_init, and the caller serialises access.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. prior prose OK; name fixed to macro-generated head

name: _n##_rb_delete
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_delete(head, node), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns the original node pointer. If node has at most one child, that child (or the sentinel) is spliced into node's place under node's parent (or head->top._f.right when the parent is the sentinel). If node has two children, the leftmost node of its right subtree (the in-order successor) is unlinked from its place and then takes over node's position: the successor's link fields are overwritten with a copy of node's (*node = *old in the code, so its parent, children and colour become node's), node's neighbours are re-pointed to the successor, and node's own link fields are left as they were. In both cases, if the colour of the node that was physically removed was black, deleteblack(head, parent, node) is called to repair the tree, and head->count is decremented; the function then returns the original node argument. It does not free memory, take locks or check that node is in the tree. head must be initialised and the caller must serialise access.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. prior prose said the successor's contents move into node; code copies the node's link fields onto the successor (ipf_rb.h:253), contents are not moved

name: _n##_rb_init
prose: Generated function _n##_rb_init(head), defined by RBI_CODE; it returns void. It zeroes the whole head structure with memset, then zeroes the per-type shared sentinel _n##_rb_zero (a global object, so initialising any head of this type resets that shared sentinel), points head->top's left and right links at the sentinel and its parent at head->top itself, and points the sentinel's left, right and parent links at itself. As a result head->count is 0 and head->compare is NULL, and the tree is empty. It allocates and frees nothing and takes no lock; calling it on a tree that is in use or while another head of the same type is in use is not safe.
note: ipf_rb.h RBI_CODE(_n, _t, _f, _cmp) macro body; the real function is _n##_rb_X generated per tree type; head->top is a dummy node whose _f.right field holds the tree root, and _n##_rb_zero is the per-type shared sentinel. added that the global sentinel is also reset

name: codel_dequeue
prose: Inline function codel_dequeue(q) is the CoDel dequeue step for dummynet queue q. It returns the mbuf it dequeued from the queue (the caller now owns it, whether or not it was ECN-marked) or NULL if the queue yielded no packet; it does not just look at the head. It reads the clock once (now = AQM_UNOW) and calls codel_dodequeue(q, now, &ok_to_drop), which removes one packet, sets ok_to_drop to 1 only when the packet's sojourn time has stayed at or above target for interval and the queue holds more than maxpkt_size bytes, and sets first_above_time as a side effect (reset to 0 when the queue is empty or the sojourn time is below target). Case dropping was true: if ok_to_drop is 0, dropping is cleared; then while now >= drop_next_time and dropping is still true, the current packet is ECN-marked if CODEL_ECN_ENABLED is set and ecn_mark(m) succeeds, in which case count is incremented, drop_next_time is advanced with control_law and that marked packet is returned immediately; otherwise the packet is dropped (update_stats(q, 0, 1) then FREE_PKT) and the next one is taken with codel_dodequeue, after which dropping is cleared if ok_to_drop is 0 and otherwise count is incremented and drop_next_time advanced with control_law. Case dropping was false and ok_to_drop is 1: unless ECN is enabled and ecn_mark succeeds on the packet, the packet is dropped (update_stats and FREE_PKT) and replaced with the result of another codel_dodequeue; in either sub-case dropping is then set true, count becomes count - 2 if count > 2 and (aqm_stime_t)now - (aqm_stime_t)drop_next_time < 8 * interval, otherwise 1, and drop_next_time is set to control_law(cst, cprms, now). Case dropping was false and ok_to_drop is 0: no further state changes beyond those made by codel_dodequeue. The packet returned at the end is the last one dequeued.
note: reviewers right: count/drop_next_time are not updated when not dropping and ok_to_drop is 0; dropping is cleared on empty queue (ok_to_drop is 0). Old prose called the result 'mbuf now at the head' which is wrong: it is the dequeued packet. dn_aqm_codel.h:131-215

name: dn_ht_scan_bucket
prose: dn_ht_scan_bucket(ht, bucket, fn, arg) scans only one hash bucket of ht. If ht or fn is NULL it returns 0 without touching anything. Otherwise, if *bucket is greater than ht->buckets it is set to 0 (this is the only change made to *bucket; the header comment about decrementing it is not implemented in the code); then the chain at ht->ht[*bucket] is walked, with the next-pointer read before fn(cur, arg) is called. If the callback result has DNHT_SCAN_DEL set, the entry is unlinked from the chain, ht->entries is decremented and a counter is incremented (the entry itself is not freed here); otherwise the walk steps past it. If the callback result has DNHT_SCAN_END set, the function returns the counter immediately after handling that entry; otherwise it returns the counter when the chain ends. The return value is the number of entries unlinked, not the number visited.
note: slice cut the head: dn_heap.c:528 dn_ht_scan_bucket (dn_heap.c:493 dn_ht_scan is the unbucketed variant)

name: do_config
prose: do_config(p, l) is the dummynet configuration entry point; p is a buffer of l bytes holding a sequence of TLV blocks, each starting with a struct dn_id. It first copies sizeof(struct dn_id) bytes from p without checking l, and returns EINVAL if o.id is not DN_API_VERSION. It then loops while l >= sizeof(struct dn_id): a block with o.len < sizeof(struct dn_id) or o.len > l sets err = EINVAL and stops; otherwise l is reduced by o.len and the block is dispatched on o.type. Unknown types are logged and skipped with err 0; DN_CMD_CONFIG is a plain header; DN_CMD_DELETE needs o.len >= sizeof(dn_id) + sizeof(uintptr_t) (else EINVAL) and reads a target from the bytes after the header: for subtype DN_LINK it takes the BH write lock, calls delete_schk(a) and delete_schk(a + DN_MAX_ID), releases the lock and returns the first non-zero result; for DN_FS it returns EINVAL if a < 1 or a >= DN_MAX_ID, otherwise delete_fs(a, 0); other subtypes give EINVAL; DN_CMD_FLUSH calls dummynet_flush() under the BH write lock; DN_TEXT frees any previous argument buffer and stores a malloc'd copy of the block (ENOMEM on failure) for later blocks; DN_LINK, DN_PROFILE, DN_SCH and DN_FS allocate one shared scratch union (ENOMEM on failure), copy a full sizeof(struct) of the matching type from the block regardless of o.len, and call config_link, config_profile, config_sched or config_fs with the saved DN_TEXT argument; for DN_FS the result is 1 (not an errno) when config_fs returns NULL. When EMULATE_SYSCTL is defined, DN_SYSCTL_SET returns kesysctl_emu_set(p, l) directly, without freeing the DN_TEXT and scratch buffers. Processing stops at the first non-zero err; on a zero err the offset advances by o.len. On normal exit both temporary buffers are freed and err is returned; if the buffer holds less than one dn_id after the first check (l < sizeof(struct dn_id)) the loop never runs and err is returned uninitialised. The input buffer p is not modified. The config_* handlers manage their own locking; do_config takes the BH write lock only around the delete-link and flush operations.
note: round1 reviewer right on contradictory precondition, wrong that function takes no lock (it takes DN_BH_WLOCK around delete link and flush, ip_dummynet.c:2080,2101); round15 reviewer right: struct sizes are copied without checking o.len (2121,2131,2142,2153); new finding: err uninitialised if l < sizeof(dn_id), and DN_SYSCTL_SET leaks buffers

name: ipfw_chk
prose: ipfw_chk(args) is the ipfw packet classifier: it decides the fate of one packet (an mbuf or a contiguous memory block, optionally with an Ethernet header) against the layer-3 rule chain and returns an IP_FW_* verdict (IP_FW_PASS, IP_FW_DENY, IP_FW_DIVERT, IP_FW_TEE, IP_FW_DUMMYNET, IP_FW_NETGRAPH, IP_FW_NGTEE, IP_FW_REASS, or a value returned by the NAT or external-action handler). The slice shown is only the tail of the function (from the O_NETGRAPH case to the end); the name do_action does not exist in ip_fw2.c. Exit paths: it returns IP_FW_PASS immediately if the mbuf has M_SKIP_FIREWALL set or V_ipfw_vnet_ready is false, and again after taking the chain read lock if V_ipfw_vnet_ready has become false; it returns IP_FW_DENY on header pullup failure (pullup_failed, printing a message when V_fw_verbose), for an IPv6 packet with an unknown routing header type, invalid single fragment header, unknown extension header or non-advertisement CARP packet when the respective denial flags apply (V_fw_deny_unknown_exthdrs, or unconditionally for CARP), and for a first-fragment-offset-1 TCP packet (RFC 3128). Otherwise it parses the headers into local variables and args->f_id, takes the chain read lock, finds the starting rule (from args->rule when IPFW_ARGS_REF is set, otherwise rule 0) and evaluates each rule's opcodes. In the tail shown: O_NETGRAPH/O_NGTEE set the match and return IP_FW_NETGRAPH or IP_FW_NGTEE; O_SETFIB, O_SETDSCP and O_SETMARK modify the mbuf fib, the IP TOS or IPv6 flow label, or the packet mark and continue with the next rule; O_NAT returns IP_FW_DENY when the packet is not IPv4, the NAT module is not loaded or no NAT instance is found, otherwise the value returned by ipfw_nat_ptr; O_REASS calls ip_reass on fragmented IPv4 packets and yields IP_FW_DENY if the fragment was swallowed or IP_FW_REASS with a fixed-up header checksum; O_EXTERNAL_ACTION returns what ipfw_run_eaction gives; an unknown opcode causes panic. When a rule action ends processing, the matched rule's counters are updated and the dtrace probe fires; if no rule ended the scan the packet is denied with a printed 'skip past end of rules' message. Before returning the verdict the chain read lock is released, a reject packet is sent with send_reject or send_reject6 if one was requested, and a cached ucred is released. Several other actions (PIPE, QUEUE, DIVERT, TEE, FORWARD_IP, DENY, REJECT, ACCEPT, SKIPTO, CALLRETURN and so on) are handled earlier in the same switch, outside this slice.
note: slice cut the head: this is a fragment of ipfw_chk (ip_fw2.c:1405-3581). Return paths verified at 1533, 1679, 1703, 1763, 1790, 1888, 3557-3580. do_action does not exist; fixed under the real name rather than dropped (rule 6)

name: list_ifaces
prose: list_ifaces(ch, op3, sd) is the ipfw sockopt handler that lists the interfaces tracked by the chain (the packet name ipfw_list_ifaces does not exist; the real function is list_ifaces in ip_fw_iface.c, the slice cut its head). It first calls ipfw_get_sopt_header(sd, sizeof(struct _ipfw_obj_lheader)); if that returns NULL, or if sd->valsize is smaller than olh->size, it returns EINVAL before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes the chain UH read lock, sets count to the number of entries in the interface object hash (0 if the chain has no such hash), computes size = count * sizeof(ipfw_iface_info) + sizeof(ipfw_obj_lheader), and fills olh->count and olh->objsize whatever the buffer size. If size > olh->size it sets olh->size = size, drops the lock and returns ENOMEM. Otherwise it sets olh->size = size, calls ipfw_objhash_foreach with export_iface_internal (one ipfw_iface_info per interface written into the sopt buffer: name, the IPFW_IFFLAG_RESOLVED flag when resolved, ifindex, refcount, generation count), drops the lock and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real name list_ifaces (ip_fw_iface.c:496); reviewer-free packet, prose checked against 505-538

name: ipfw_check_opcode
prose: ipfw_check_opcode(pcmd, plen, ci) validates one instruction of a rule body and returns an enum ipfw_opcheck_result: SUCCESS, CHECK_ACTION, BAD_SIZE or FAILED. It reads the instruction at *pcmd and its length F_LEN, and for most opcodes returns BAD_SIZE when the length does not equal the size that opcode requires (or, for O_IP_SRC_MASK/O_IP_DST_MASK and the IPv6 mask opcodes, when the length is even; for O_NOP, O_IPID and similar when it is outside 1..31; for O_MAC_TYPE and the port opcodes outside 2..31). Opcodes that only match (for example O_PROTO, O_IN, O_IP_SRC) return SUCCESS after the size check. Side effects on ci on non-error paths: ci->object_opcodes is incremented for O_PROBE_STATE, O_KEEP_STATE, O_EXTERNAL_ACTION, O_LIMIT, the table lookup opcodes, O_RECV/O_XMIT/O_VIA and O_CHECK_STATE and for the O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE that may follow an external action; IPFW_RCIFLAG_HAS_STATE is set in ci->flags only by O_PROBE_STATE and O_KEEP_STATE; O_LOG sets log_left to max_log; a lookup instruction of the ipfw_insn_table size gets the lookup-masking flag when its lookup type is not LOOKUP_NONE and the match-table-value flag otherwise. FAILED is returned for: a zero kidx on O_EXTERNAL_ACTION or its following O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE; an instruction after O_EXTERNAL_ACTION that is neither O_EXTERNAL_DATA nor O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE; O_FIB with arg1 >= rt_numfibs; O_SETFIB with arg1 not IP_FW_TARG and (arg1 & 0x7FFF) >= rt_numfibs; O_IP_SRC_SET/O_IP_DST_SET with arg1 equal to 0 or above 256; a lookup or O_TABLE_LOOKUP kidx >= V_fw_tables_max; O_DIVERT/O_TEE when ip_divert_ptr is NULL; O_NETGRAPH/O_NGTEE when ng_ipfw_input_p is NULL; O_NAT when the NAT module is not loaded; the bad_targ cases, where tablearg (IP_FW_TARG) is used while HAS_STATE is already set, which apply to O_SETFIB, O_PIPE, O_QUEUE, O_DIVERT, O_TEE, O_NETGRAPH, O_NGTEE, O_NAT, O_SETDSCP, O_SKIPTO and O_SETMARK (checked on d[0] for the last two), and O_CALLRETURN unless F_NOT marks it as a return, and for O_FORWARD_IP with address INADDR_ANY; any unknown opcode; and IPv6 opcodes when the kernel has no INET6. CHECK_ACTION is returned for the action opcodes: O_EXTERNAL_ACTION (also after an O_EXTERNAL_DATA or valid O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE follows it), O_SETFIB, O_PIPE, O_QUEUE, O_FORWARD_IP, O_FORWARD_IP6, O_DIVERT, O_TEE, O_NETGRAPH, O_NGTEE, O_NAT, O_SKIPTO, O_CALLRETURN, O_SETMARK, O_CHECK_STATE, O_FORWARD_MAC, O_COUNT, O_ACCEPT, O_DENY, O_REJECT, O_SETDSCP, O_UNREACH6 and O_REASS, after the size check. For O_EXTERNAL_ACTION, if *plen differs from the instruction length it first subtracts that length from *plen and advances *pcmd to the next instruction; this happens before the next instruction is examined, so it also takes effect on the FAILED and BAD_SIZE returns that follow (a wrong-size O_EXTERNAL_INSTANCE gives BAD_SIZE; the size of a following O_EXTERNAL_DATA is not checked). All other paths leave *pcmd and *plen unchanged.
note: round1 right (bad_targ FAILED for O_SETFIB with IP_FW_TARG when HAS_STATE set); round2 wrong about the return code (O_SETFIB returns CHECK_ACTION in old prose too, ip_fw_sockopt.c:1419); round15 right (O_EXTERNAL_ACTION advances *pcmd/*plen before BAD_SIZE/FAILED returns, 1377-1393). Checked all cases 1326-1685

name: nat64_do_handle_ip6
prose: nat64_do_handle_ip6(m, aaddr, aport, cfg, logdata) translates one IPv6 packet to IPv4 for NAT64 and sends it out. The slice named nat64_translate; the real function is nat64_do_handle_ip6 in nat64_translate.c:1558 and the slice cut its head. It returns NAT64SKIP, without freeing or counting anything, if the IPv6 source or destination fails nat64_check_ip6. It returns NAT64MFREE (the caller must free the mbuf) after incrementing cfg->stats dropped when: the IPv4 source aaddr fails nat64_check_ip4; the IPv4 destination extracted from the IPv6 destination with cfg->plat_plen is 0; nat64_getlasthdr returns a negative protocol; the fragment header is not contiguous in the first mbuf; the protocol after a fragment header is ICMPv6; or the payload length is negative or larger than the mbuf. It returns NAT64RETURN, with the mbuf consumed, after nat64_icmp6_reflect for: hop limit <= IPV6_HLIMDEC (only when *V_nat64ip6stealth is 0, ICMP6_TIME_EXCEEDED); a fragment with the more-fragments flag whose length is not a multiple of 8 octets (ICMP6_PARAM_PROB); no IPv4 route to the destination (noroute4 counted, ICMP6_DST_UNREACH); or nh_mtu < plen + sizeof(struct ip) (ICMP6_PACKET_TOO_BIG). For an ICMPv6 payload whose type is neither echo request nor echo reply it returns whatever nat64_handle_icmp6 returns. Otherwise it builds the IPv4 header, completes a delayed IPv6 checksum if needed, converts the TCP, UDP or ICMPv6 echo checksum (replacing the source port or ICMP id with aport when aport is non-zero and changing the ICMPv6 echo type to the ICMP echo type), trims the mbuf to the new header, calls V_nat64out->output, increments opcnt64 if that returned 0, and returns NAT64RETURN regardless of the output result.
note: reviewer round15 right: hop-limit reflection depends on *V_nat64ip6stealth == 0 (nat64_translate.c:1596). Also found NAT64SKIP path (1576-1579) missing from earlier prose; real name nat64_do_handle_ip6

name: pfsync_in_clr
prose: pfsync_in_clr(m, offset, count, flags, action) handles a pfsync 'clear states' message. Each record is a struct pfsync_clr of IFNAMSIZ + 4 bytes (a 16-byte interface name and a 32-bit creatorid, packed, 20 bytes). It calls m_pulldown(m, offset, 20 * count, &offp); if that returns NULL it increments pfsyncs_badlen and returns -1 (it does not free m and takes no lock; the caller releases the rules lock and does not free m on this path). Otherwise, for each of the count records, the record is skipped if its ifname is non-empty and pfi_kkif_find(ifname) returns NULL; for the remaining records it scans every row of the state ID hash (0..V_pf_hashmask), taking the row lock, and for each state whose creatorid equals the record's it sets PFSTATE_NOSYNC and calls pf_remove_state, then restarts the scan of that row (goto relock) until no state with that creatorid remains in the row, and releases the row lock. The interface name is only checked for existence; it is not used to restrict which states are removed. The function returns 20 * count, the number of payload bytes consumed, and holds no row lock on return. The caller (pfsync_input) is expected to hold PF_RULES_RLOCK.
note: reviewers round2 and round15 right: sizeof(struct pfsync_clr) is IFNAMSIZ(16)+4 = 20 bytes, packed (net/if_pfsync.h:140), not 24; round1 claim concerns the caller, which indeed returns IPPROTO_DONE on -1 without m_freem (if_pfsync.c:1127-1129), consistent with this prose (m not freed)

name: pf_purge_expired_states
prose: pf_purge_expired_states(i, maxcheck) is called only from the pf purge thread and scans up to maxcheck rows of the state ID hash starting at row i. It first sets V_pf_status.states from the state zone's current count. While maxcheck > 0 it takes row i: if the row's state list is non-empty it takes the row lock and walks it; a state whose expiry (pf_state_expires) is not after time_uptime is removed with pf_remove_state (V_pf_status.states is decremented by its result) and the walk of that row restarts after re-taking the lock; every other state has its rule, nat rule, anchor, match rules, interface and route interface marked with PFRULE_REFS or PFI_IFLAG_REFS reference flags. The row lock is released, then i is incremented; if i has passed V_pf_hashmask the function sets V_pf_status.states again from the zone count and returns 0 (a wrap to the start); otherwise maxcheck is decremented and the loop continues. When maxcheck reaches 0 it refreshes V_pf_status.states and returns i, which is the first row not scanned: the starting i plus the number of rows scanned. If maxcheck <= 0 on entry no row is scanned and i is returned unchanged. No row lock is held on return.
note: reviewers round2 right (maxcheck <= 0 returns i unchanged, may be 0) and original review right that the formal ensures was imprecise; contract dropped because the function reads/writes global state (V_pf_idhash, V_pf_status). pf.c:2907-2962

name: pf_test_state_icmp
prose: pf_test_state_icmp(state, pd, reason) matches an ICMP or ICMPv6 packet against pf state; *state must be NULL on entry (MPASS) and pd->proto must be IPPROTO_ICMP or IPPROTO_ICMPV6 (any other value panics; the real pf.c name and head are at pf.c:7908). It returns a pf action: PF_PASS, PF_DROP, PF_AFRT, or a non-match action passed through from pf_icmp_state_lookup or pf_find_state. Query/reply branch (pf_icmp_mapping returns 0): it looks up an ICMP state with pf_icmp_state_lookup (retrying with a multicast match for an outbound IPv6 packet after PF_DROP); if the lookup returns a non-negative action that action is returned with *state NULL. Otherwise it refreshes (*state)->expire and sets timeout to PFTM_ICMP_ERROR_REPLY, and if the state's wire and stack keys differ it rewrites the addresses (pf_change_a or pf_change_a6) and the ICMP id in the packet and copies the header back, returning PF_DROP if an address-family translation (pf_translate_icmp_af) fails (no *reason set), PF_AFRT after a successful family translation, and otherwise PF_PASS. Error branch: it extracts the inner IP header and the inner protocol headers (pf_pull_hdr, pf_walk_header or pf_walk_header6), returning PF_DROP with a reason set by those helpers (or PFRES_FRAG when the inner IPv4 header is a non-first fragment); it returns PF_DROP with PFRES_BADSTATE if the outer destination does not equal the inner source. The inner packet is then looked up by protocol: TCP (state found with pf_find_state, sequence checked against the peer window unless PFSTATE_SLOPPY, giving PF_DROP with PFRES_BADSTATE if outside), UDP, SCTP (PF_DROP without reason if the verification tag differs), inner ICMP and ICMPv6 (PF_DROP with PFRES_NORM if the inner family is wrong), and a default case for other protocols, each returning the non-PF_MATCH action from the lookup or, on a match, translating addresses and ports in the inner and outer headers (with checksum fixups and m_copyback) when the state keys differ; a failed family translation returns PF_DROP without setting *reason, and a successful one returns PF_AFRT, otherwise PF_PASS. On a PF_DROP that happens after a state was found, *state is left pointing at the state.
note: reviewer round15 right: PF_DROP from pf_translate_icmp_af / pf_change_icmp_af failure sets no *reason (pf.c:7995, 8290-8300). Old claim '*state left NULL otherwise' is wrong for DROP after a state was found; summary-level description of a ~1000-line function

name: pf_altq_ifnet_event
prose: pf_altq_ifnet_event(ifp, remove) rebuilds the ALTQ configuration after an interface event; it returns void. The caller is expected to hold the PF rules write lock. It returns doing nothing if ALTQ_IS_READY(&ifp->if_snd) is false. Otherwise it rolls back an open inactive altq set (pf_rollback_altq with the inactive ticket) if V_altqs_inactive_open is set, and starts a new transaction with pf_begin_altq; if pf_begin_altq fails it returns with no further change. It then copies each entry of the active altq_if list into a malloc'd (M_NOWAIT) pf_altq (ENOMEM and stop on allocation failure), passes it to pf_altq_ifnet_event_add and, if that returns 0, appends it to the inactive interface list. pf_altq_ifnet_event_add marks the copy PFALTQ_FLAG_IF_REMOVED when the interface name no longer resolves or when remove is non-zero and it is the event interface; otherwise it calls altq_add, then returns EBUSY if the ticket no longer equals V_ticket_altqs_inactive, and frees the copy if either altq_add or the ticket check produced an error. If the first loop fails, it goes to the rollback. Otherwise it does the same for each entry of the active altq (queue) list, but first assigns the copy a queue id with pf_qname2qid (a zero result frees the copy and sets EBUSY) and sets altq_disc from the matching-interface entry of the new inactive interface list or NULL; successful copies are appended to the inactive queue list. On any error it calls pf_rollback_altq(ticket) to discard the partially built inactive sets; with no error it calls pf_commit_altq(ticket) and ignores its return value, so a commit failure is not reported.
note: reviewers right: round15 (altq_add failure frees the copy and aborts) and round2 (IF_REMOVED only if interface missing or remove && same ifp), original review right (early return when pf_begin_altq fails, commit result ignored). pf_ioctl.c:1149-1247

name: pf_load
prose: pf_load() is the pf module load handler (static, no parameters). It initialises the pf_end_lock sx lock and calls pf_mtag_initialize(), then creates the /dev/pf character device with make_dev(&pf_cdevsw, 0, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0600, PF_NAME). If make_dev returns NULL it returns ENOMEM; the lock initialisation and mtag initialisation are not undone. Otherwise it sets pf_end_threads to 0 and creates the 'pf purge' kernel process with kproc_create(pf_purge_thread, ..., &pf_purge_proc, ...); if that returns a non-zero error it returns that error (pf_dev stays created and pfi_initialize is not called). Otherwise it calls pfi_initialize() and returns 0.
note: pf_ioctl.c:7088-7109; contract dropped (writes global state and the old contract was malformed)

name: pf_normalize_tcp
prose: pf_normalize_tcp(pd) applies TCP scrubbing to the segment described by pd and returns PF_PASS or PF_DROP. It asserts the rules read lock (PF_RULES_RASSERT). It walks the active scrub ruleset (counting r->evaluations for each rule visited) to find the first matching rule rm, using skip steps on interface, direction, address family, protocol, source and destination address and port, and OS fingerprint. If at least one scrub rule exists and either no rule matched or the matched rule's action is PF_NOSCRUB, it returns PF_PASS without changing the packet. If a rule matched and is not PF_NOSCRUB it adds the packet and byte counters of that rule and copies the rule's actions into pd->act. If there are no scrub rules at all, normalization still proceeds with rm == NULL. If rm has PFRULE_REASSEMBLE_TCP, PFDESC_TCP_NORM is set in pd->flags. It then returns PF_DROP when the TCP flags are illegal: SYN with RST or with FIN; a segment without SYN that has neither ACK nor RST; FIN, PUSH or URG without ACK; or when th_off is below sizeof(struct tcphdr)/4 words (5). On a drop it computes reason = PFRES_NORM in a local variable only (no reason is returned to the caller) and logs the packet through PFLOG_PACKET when rm is non-NULL and the rule has logging. Otherwise it returns PF_PASS after possibly sanitising the header: the condition for clearing reserved bits tests TH_RES1 and TH_RES2 (TH_RES2 is tested twice and TH_RES3 is not tested), so a segment with only TH_RES3 set is not changed by this step; when it does trigger, TH_RES1, TH_RES2 and TH_RES3 are all cleared and the checksum is adjusted; a non-zero urgent pointer without TH_URG is zeroed with a checksum adjustment; and if either change was made the TCP header is copied back to the mbuf with m_copyback.
note: reviewers right: round15 (TH_RES3 omitted from the test, pf_norm.c:1469, while the clear at 1473 includes it), round2 (PF_PASS when no scrub rule matches or NOSCRUB), original (th_off < 5 drop). Also old prose said '*reason set' but reason is a local variable (1384, 1496)

name: pf_normalize_sctp
prose: pf_normalize_sctp(pd) applies SCTP scrubbing and returns PF_PASS or PF_DROP; it never modifies the packet. It asserts the rules read lock, then walks the active scrub rules, incrementing r->evaluations for each rule it visits (so counters are touched even when it later returns PF_PASS without normalizing), looking for the first rule that matches interface, direction, address family, protocol, addresses and ports. If at least one scrub rule exists and either no rule matched or the matched rule's action is PF_NOSCRUB, it returns PF_PASS. If a rule matched and is not PF_NOSCRUB, that rule's packet and byte counters for the packet's direction are incremented. When there are no scrub rules at all the checks below still run. It returns PF_DROP if (pd->tot_len - pd->off - sizeof(struct sctphdr)) is not a multiple of 4, or if PFDESC_SCTP_INIT is set together with any other bit in pd->sctp_flags. On a drop, reason = PFRES_NORM is set in a local variable, the packet is logged with PFLOG_PACKET if a rule matched and has logging enabled, and PF_DROP is returned. Otherwise it returns PF_PASS.
note: reviewers: original right that scrub rules do not themselves reject; round2 right (checks still run with no scrub rules); round15 right (evaluations incremented for every rule walked, pf_norm.c:2151). pf_norm.c:2136-2208

name: pf_validate_op
prose: pf_validate_op(op) checks that op is one of the pf comparison operators PF_OP_NONE, PF_OP_IRG, PF_OP_EQ, PF_OP_NE, PF_OP_LT, PF_OP_LE, PF_OP_GT, PF_OP_GE, PF_OP_XRG, PF_OP_RRG (the values 0 through 9). It returns 0 for those values and EINVAL (22) for every other uint8_t value. It reads and writes no memory.
note: pf_nv.c:373-393; enum in netpfil/pf/pf.h:55

name: pf_syncookies_setmode
prose: pf_syncookies_setmode(mode) sets the pf syncookie mode. It returns EINVAL if mode is greater than PF_SYNCOOKIES_MODE_MAX (PF_SYNCOOKIES_ADAPTIVE, 2) and changes nothing. If mode equals V_pf_status.syncookies_mode it returns 0 with no change. Otherwise it stores mode in V_pf_status.syncookies_mode and, if the new mode is PF_SYNCOOKIES_ALWAYS, calls pf_syncookie_newkey() and sets V_pf_status.syncookies_active to true; it then returns 0. It does not take any lock itself; it reads and writes the vnet pf status.
note: pf_syncookies.c:243-258; contract dropped because the function reads and writes global pf state

name: pfr_ina_define
prose: pfr_ina_define(tbl, addr, size, nadd, naddr, ticket, flags) defines a table, with an optional address list, inside an open table transaction. It asserts the rules write lock. It returns EINVAL if flags has any bit outside PFR_FLAG_DUMMY | PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO (ACCEPT_FLAGS), if size is non-zero but PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO is not set, or if pfr_validate_table rejects tbl; it returns EBUSY if the ruleset for tbl->pfrt_anchor does not exist, is not open for tables, or ticket differs from the ruleset's table ticket. None of these early returns changes anything. After them it sets PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE in the caller's tbl->pfrt_flags. It looks up the table in the global tree; if absent, it creates it (ENOMEM on failure), counts it in xadd, and for a table in an anchor looks up or creates a root table (ENOMEM on failure, destroying the already created table); if the table exists but is not currently PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE it is counted in xadd. It then creates a shadow table (ENOMEM on failure, destroying the work list) and, for each of the size addresses, returns EINVAL if pfr_validate_addr rejects it, skips duplicates, creates and routes an entry (ENOMEM if creation fails, silently skipping entries that fail to route), counting each added entry in xaddr. Any of those errors after the shadow was created destroys the shadow table, the new tables and the new entries and returns the error. If flags lacks PFR_FLAG_DUMMY the previous shadow of kt (if any) is destroyed, PFR_TFLAG_INACTIVE is set on kt, the newly created tables are inserted into the global tree, shadow->pfrkt_cnt is set to xaddr if PFR_FLAG_ADDRSTOO was given and to NO_ADDRESSES otherwise, and the shadow is installed as kt->pfrkt_shadow. If PFR_FLAG_DUMMY is set, the shadow table, new tables and entries are destroyed and nothing is installed. On success it stores xadd in *nadd and xaddr in *naddr when those pointers are non-NULL (also for the dummy case) and returns 0.
note: reviewers right: round15 (tbl->pfrt_flags INACTIVE is set only after the EINVAL/EBUSY checks, pf_table.c:1540); round2 prose already agrees with code (xadd counts new tables and existing non-inactive tables); original right (shadow installed only when not DUMMY, 1592-1605)

name: audit_send_trigger
prose: audit_send_trigger(trigger) queues an audit trigger value for the userspace audit daemon. It first allocates a struct trigger_info with malloc(M_WAITOK), which may sleep, before taking audit_trigger_mtx. It then takes audit_trigger_mtx; if audit_isopen is false (no reader has opened the audit device) it releases the mutex, frees the allocation and returns ENODEV, leaving trigger_list unchanged. Otherwise it stores trigger in the entry, appends the entry to the tail of trigger_list, calls selwakeup on audit_trigger_rsel and wakeup on trigger_list, releases the mutex and returns 0. The queued entry is later removed and freed by audit_read or audit_close; the caller gets no reference to it. The caller must not hold audit_trigger_mtx.
note: audit_trigger.c:147-166; contract dropped (function modifies global queue state)

name: mac_proc_vm_revoke_recurse
prose: mac_proc_vm_revoke_recurse(td, cred, map) revokes memory-map permissions that MAC policy no longer allows for a process, in map and recursively in its sub-maps; it returns void. If mac_mmap_revocation is false it returns immediately without touching the map. Otherwise it takes the map lock (vm_map_lock) and visits each map entry: for a sub-map entry it calls itself on the sub-map and continues; an entry with MAP_ENTRY_COW or MAP_ENTRY_NOSYNC set or with zero max_protection, with a NULL object, or whose deepest backing object is not OBJT_VNODE is skipped. For a vnode-backed entry it locks the vnode, calls mac_vnode_check_mmap_downgrade to get the permissions still allowed, and computes revokeperms = max_protection & ~result; if that is empty the entry is skipped; otherwise it prints a message with the pid and the revoked permissions. If the entry's current protection does not include any revoked permission, only max_protection is reduced by revokeperms. Otherwise: when write is revoked it takes a temporary reference on the object, starts a vnode write and cleans the object's pages for the entry's range (vm_object_page_clean with OBJPC_SYNC under the vnode and object locks), then releases the locks and the reference; it clears VM_PROT_WRITE from max_protection and protection unless mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow is set, and independently of mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow sets MAP_ENTRY_COW | MAP_ENTRY_NEEDS_COPY when read is not being revoked; when execute is revoked it clears VM_PROT_EXECUTE from both max_protection and protection; when read is revoked both are set to 0; it then calls pmap_protect on the entry's range with protection & ~revokeperms and vm_map_try_merge_entries with the previous entry. It finishes by releasing the map lock with vm_map_unlock.
note: reviewers right: round15 (COW/NEEDS_COPY is set whenever read is not revoked regardless of mac_mmap_revocation_via_cow: the '} if' at mac_process.c:352 is a separate if), round2 (early return when mac_mmap_revocation is false), original (via_cow leaves write max_protection)

name: mac_sysvmsq_check_msqrcv
prose: mac_sysvmsq_check_msqrcv(cred, msqkptr) asks the MAC framework whether credential cred may receive from the SysV message queue msqkptr. It runs MAC_POLICY_CHECK_NOSLEEP(sysvmsq_check_msqrcv, cred, msqkptr, msqkptr->label) and then the probe macro MAC_CHECK_PROBE2, and returns the resulting error. The macro calls the sysvmsq_check_msqrcv entry point of every policy that defines one: the static policy list without a lock, and, if the dynamic policy list is not empty, the dynamic list while holding a non-sleeping read lock on the policy list (mac_policy_slock_nosleep), released before return. It does not stop at the first failing policy; the individual results are combined with mac_error_select, which gives precedence to EDEADLK, EINVAL, ESRCH, ENOENT, EACCES and EPERM in that order, then to any other non-zero error, so the result is 0 only if every policy that defines the entry point returned 0. The probe does not change the returned value. It acquires and releases no references.
note: reviewer right: the dynamic-policy path takes the policy list read lock (mac_internal.h:311-322), so 'no locks are taken' was false; also the old prose 'first nonzero error' is wrong: errors are merged with mac_error_select (mac_framework.c:700)

name: maybe_demote
prose: maybe_demote(subjlabel, objlabel, actionname, objname, vp) demotes the current process's LOMAC label after it has accessed a lower-level object, and logs the demotion; it returns 0 on both of its returns. It takes subj = the process label slot of curthread's process and locks subj->mtx. If subj->mac_lomac has MAC_LOMAC_FLAG_UPDATE set (a demotion already pending) and lomac_dominate_single(objlabel, &subj->mac_lomac) is true, that is, objlabel's single label dominates the pending single label, it unlocks the mutex and returns 0 leaving the pending label unchanged and logging nothing. Otherwise it zeroes subj->mac_lomac, copies objlabel's single into it (objlabel must have a single label), copies subjlabel's range into it (subjlabel must have a range), sets the range low to objlabel's single only if objlabel's single does not dominate that low element (otherwise the low stays that of subjlabel), sets the range high to objlabel's single, sets MAC_LOMAC_FLAG_UPDATE and schedules a TDA_MAC AST with ast_sched. It then caches the single label in a local, unlocks subj->mtx, builds three sbuf strings (subject label, new label read from subj->mac_lomac after the unlock, object label), and logs a LOG_INFO message that includes the inode number and mount point when vp is non-NULL and VOP_GETATTR succeeds, or without them otherwise. It deletes the three sbufs and returns 0.
note: reviewers right: round15 (low endpoint is replaced by the object's single only when the object's single does NOT dominate the low, mac_lomac.c:527-529); original/round1 (code keeps the pending label when the object dominates it, 511-514). Old prose about 'objlabel's range high' was wrong: the test is lomac_dominate_single(objlabel, pending label)

name: name##_ARB_CFIND
prose: Generated function name_ARB_CFIND(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_CFIND (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning a const pointer to a node of the tree whose key compares equal (cmp(elm, node) == 0) to elm's key, or NULL if there is none. It descends from the root using the left/right indices and never modifies the tree.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_FIND
prose: Generated function name_ARB_FIND(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_FIND (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning the same node as name##_ARB_CFIND(head, elm) with the const qualifier removed (via __DECONST), or NULL if there is none. It does not modify the tree.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_CNFIND
prose: Generated function name_ARB_CNFIND(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_CNFIND (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning a const pointer to the node with the smallest key that is greater than or equal to elm's key (an equal node is returned as soon as it is found), or NULL if every node's key is smaller than elm's. It does not modify the tree.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_NFIND
prose: Generated function name_ARB_NFIND(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_NFIND (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning the node returned by name##_ARB_CNFIND(head, elm) with the const qualifier removed, so the smallest node with key >= elm's key, or NULL if there is none. It does not modify the tree.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_CNEXT
prose: Generated function name_ARB_CNEXT(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_CNEXT (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning a const pointer to the in-order successor of elm computed from the child and parent indices (the leftmost node of elm's right subtree if there is one, otherwise the nearest ancestor reached from a left child), or NULL if elm is the last node. elm must be a node stored in head's node array.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_NEXT
prose: Generated function name_ARB_NEXT(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_NEXT (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning the node returned by name##_ARB_CNEXT(head, elm) with the const qualifier removed: the in-order successor of elm, or NULL if elm is the last node. elm must be a node stored in head's node array.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_CPREV
prose: Generated function name_ARB_CPREV(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_CPREV (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning a const pointer to the in-order predecessor of elm computed from the child and parent indices (the rightmost node of elm's left subtree if there is one, otherwise the nearest ancestor reached from a right child), or NULL if elm is the first node. elm must be a node stored in head's node array.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_PREV
prose: Generated function name_ARB_PREV(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_PREV (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning the node returned by name##_ARB_CPREV(head, elm) with the const qualifier removed: the in-order predecessor of elm, or NULL if elm is the first node. elm must be a node stored in head's node array.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_CMINMAX
prose: Generated function name_ARB_CMINMAX(head, val), defined by ARB_GENERATE_CMINMAX (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning NULL if the tree is empty (ARB_EMPTY: no current nodes); otherwise it walks from the root and returns a const pointer to the leftmost (minimum) node when val < 0 and to the rightmost (maximum) node when val >= 0.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_MINMAX
prose: Generated function name_ARB_MINMAX(head, val), defined by ARB_GENERATE_MINMAX (inside the ARB_GENERATE family of macros in sys/arb.h) and returning the pointer returned by name##_ARB_CMINMAX(head, val) with the const qualifier removed: NULL for an empty tree, the leftmost node when val < 0, otherwise the rightmost node.
note: sys/arb.h:563-693

name: name##_ARB_REINSERT
prose: Generated function name_ARB_REINSERT(head, elm), defined by ARB_GENERATE_REINSERT. It checks the ordering of elm against its in-order neighbours using name_ARB_PREV and name_ARB_NEXT: if the predecessor exists and cmp(prev, elm) >= 0, or the successor exists and cmp(elm, next) >= 0, the position is wrong. If the position is still strictly ordered it returns NULL and leaves the tree unchanged. Otherwise it calls name_ARB_REMOVE(head, elm), which returns the node to the free list, takes a node from the free list with ARB_GETFREE(head, field) and returns the result of name_ARB_INSERT(head, node): NULL when the node was inserted, or a pointer to an existing node whose key compares equal if there is one (in which case nothing is inserted). It therefore returns NULL both when nothing needed to be done and when the re-insertion succeeded; it does not return the inserted node.
note: prior prose wrong: ARB_GENERATE_INSERT returns NULL on success and the colliding node on a duplicate key (arb.h:537, 560); the 'returns the inserted node' claim is false. arb.h:695-711
